newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW - French unemployment falls in March.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - French unemployment falls in March.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on French unemployment, which fell a seasonally adjusted 4,800 in March, with the ILO jobless rate stuck at a record 12.8 percent, according to labour ministry data on Wednesday.
In an electoral campaign environment these figures have to be taken with a pinch of salt. It looks like unemployment data is not meant to interfere wit the campaign.
Needless to say in the current environment these figures are of little informative value.
SEAN SHEPLEY, INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIST, CS FIRST BOSTON:

It's not quite as stark as in the U.K. but it's the same situation in that the headline numbers are not behaving in the same way as the ILO numbers. It's clear the labour market in France is still pretty soft.

Although it's convenient to able to point to a headline number now turning down, the sense to give is that employment growth is not picking up strongly as long as domestic demand remains fairly depressed.
It avoids disaster. Clearly unemployment rising strongly going into the election would have been negative.
SONJA GIBBS, BOND ANALYST, NOMURA INTERNATIONAL

I think it's very good news for the government that we've had second successive monthly fall. Whatever the economic impact, the political and psychological impact is positive. I think most economists would be slightly sceptical of a turnaround so soon...after the next couple of months it could stagnate again.
